description: This line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC %) of six different methods—Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME—on Llama3 as a function of the co-occurrence number, which is plotted on a logarithmic x-axis ranging from 0 to approximately 10⁴. The y-axis represents ACC (%) on a linear scale from 60% to 80%, with major gridlines at 60, 65, 70, 75, and 80. The Base method (black line with circle markers) starts at ~61% and gradually increases to ~67%. The FT method (blue line with downward triangle markers) begins at ~62.5% and rises to ~68.5%. The IKE method (red line with upward triangle markers) starts at ~64.5% and reaches ~70%. The MEND method (brown line with diamond markers) begins at ~66.5% and climbs to ~74%. The MEMIT method (purple line with circle markers) starts at ~66.5% and increases to ~72.5%. The ROME method (green line with square markers) starts at ~72.5% and plateaus near 78% for higher co-occurrence numbers. All methods show a general upward trend in accuracy as co-occurrence number increases, with ROME consistently outperforming the others across the range.
